title: Rikitake's two-disc dynamo is chaotic: a computer-assisted proof
description:
In plain words. A planet's magnetic field can flip, north becoming south. In 1958 Tsuneji Rikitake proposed the simplest mechanical model of such flipping: two spinning copper discs, each driving current through the other's coil. In simulations its polarity reverses at irregular moments, and since a 1980 numerical study it has been called chaotic; as far as we could find, that had never been proved. This archive proves that the model has chaotic motions at three parameter settings, with two separately written checking programs. The theorem says nothing about most starting points, or about what a typical simulation settles into.

The idea in one picture. kneading dough. A baker stretches the dough long, lays it back across itself and stretches it again. Here the dough is the set of possible states of the dynamo, and one loop of its motion does the stretching. We picked two thin boxes of states, one whose next loop brings no reversal and one whose next loop does reverse, and proved that one loop stretches each box right across the boxes it leads to. Where the picture breaks. a baker mixes all the dough, but the stretching is proved only for these two thin boxes.

For specialists. The Rikitake two-disc dynamo (1958), the classic minimal model of geomagnetic polarity reversals, has been called chaotic since Ito's 1980 numerical study but its chaos had not been proved. For three parameter values we prove, with rigorous interval-arithmetic Poincare maps (CAPD), covering relations for the symmetry-reduced return map to a plane section. Consequently every reversal pattern with no two consecutive non-reversal loops is realised by a true solution, there are infinitely many periodic orbits, and the return map has topological entropy at least log of the golden ratio. Two independently written checkers, a known-result control and a negative control are included.

Links. Repository, with a plain-language guide: github.com/Hashirama1337s/rikitake-chaos. All projects: the Moki & Julio lab map.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
